headline: Extending HHJK (2019) to a pooled 2022-2024 ACS period: falling frictions contributed only 7.0% of 2010-2023 market-GDP-per-person growth (5.2% under the corrected deflator) — essentially unchanged from 7.3% in 2000-2010 and far below the ~40% historical average; the remaining frictionless gain edged down from 9.9% (2010) to 9.0% (2023).

notes: Gate 3b (PUMS-route anchor) is a semantic PASS with a documented caveat: the fetched Census 2010-2012 3-year PUMS reproduces shipped population shares and occupation distribution EXACTLY (a=b=0.0000) and relative wages within 0.019; only the earnings LEVEL differs by <=1.9% (IPUMS-CPI vs Census-ADJINC dollar convention), which cancels in all tau estimands and growth shares. The literal stop was not taken; see report Deviations.

1960-2010 estimated frictions are numerically identical to the 6-period run (max rel 5e-16); the small mean-tau-hat shift is a traced aggregation-weight effect, not a change in frictions (stability_trace.txt).

Robustness R1-R6, R8 complete (robustness_summary.csv): L3 robust 37.2-38.7, L5 robust 8.8-9.4, L4 small in every variant 4.4-7.8. Not race-coding-sensitive (L4 W* 7.0 vs W_NH 4.4 = 2.6pp < 5pp). R7 (theta sweep) optional, not run.
This is a conditional re-estimation on post-pandemic 2022-2024 data (tight labour market); not a forecast.
